And know that the misstep of he who is felled by his own candor cannot be excused.

The sensible man
treats his enemy with whom he reconciled with some of his previous reserve and does not trust him fully.

p.n: The Best Thing Is Distance From the Enemy

body.p:
Neither does he trust him with his safety,
when he approaches him and stays away from him as much as he can.

The Chapter of the King and the Bird Fanza Qatra
King Dayshalam said to the Philosopher Baydhabā: “I have heard this parable. Present to me the parable of
harm inflicted, in which the one cannot avoid meeting the other. Baydhabā said: “They claim that
a King of Indian Royalty called Badrīn had a bird called Fanza, which had a nestling. This
bird and its nestling spoke eloquently, and the King admired them. So he ordered
they be placed with his wife and ordered her to look after them. It so happened that the King’s wife
gave birth to a boy, and she said, ‘This nestling will rear my child-both are younglings and they will play together!’
